constraints: All active TP8 graph and eager targets at source layers 2,8,14,20,24,28,32,36. 30 reuse layers consume previously published lists and two SWA-only layers carry no new selection. An empty-Q rank can still send/receive or write C2 state. Keep its actual outgoing packet readiness. Endpoints use the favorable active DP, local savings propagate to the sender, peer comparison at original send transpose end and unchanged downstream time. Cross-rank offset bounds come from each wave; aligned export is a separate assumption. Request deadlines count the eligible current wave. No measured end-to-end speedup.

C2 pairs are two 512-wide FP32 inputs. Potential co-read charged only on up to the last 32 rows per request and capped by original pool/update. Fusing pool to RMS may remove a BF16 write/read per materialized row if other readers retired. Keep original zero/default payload, full FP32 ring, completed BF16 boundary and necessary math; alias and even predecessor guards from original native fixtures apply. Even-only storage and scheduling-only update/RMS overlap have separate scenarios. Fully free old pool group also removes necessary work. The direct 4096 bytes per tail row is one duplicate read; it is not all prefill rows. Projection fusion may additionally remove an FP32 4096-byte write and first read per live row if both original rounding boundaries and the pool/ring consumers are preserved. Counts all live rows as read, a favorable sensitivity.

512 INT32 positions per query. Remove at most a raw store/read between QLI and the ordered-list builder and one first attention read. Subsequent readers retain sorted output, lengths and candidate packet. These are logical bytes at calibrated bandwidth. Index-key and compressed BF16 KV remain distinct. Old QLI candidate copy/time and the earlier QLI implementation measured on another service are not added to this budget.

Query tiling uses the pinned per-sequence QLI four-row base and up to four waves of completed groups. For small nonuniform batches we allow the most favorable request order, within contiguous SP shards. Ignore graph pad-only query rows for grouping; for a partial last shard the measured stage duration may include padding. Stage one includes the original QLI and preparation, stage two SMLA. The model allocates equal time per live row within each operator and allows stage two to start only once a full ordered result is available. Keep per-query tie/filler order, reusable publication and original SMLA arithmetic. This cap of four publication waves is a modeled schedule, not a ceiling over arbitrary tile counts. One-row retiling is a separate ideal sensitivity. No early finality from partial keys. Multi-core partials must complete their final reduction; no current per-group notification or numeric acceptance is asserted.

Half and quarter overlap are sensitivity parameters for useful concurrent execution, including shared Cube/vector/GM pressure. Paid arms charge 2 us per extra handoff (scenario, not a measured event). At fixed tile order only the disjoint eliminated index handoff is attributed to fusion; overlap is separately conditional on tiled scheduling. Native baseline is the frozen archived capture prior to repaired QLI. Cache work for other layers is not moved into a query tile.

Ordinary projections interpolate prompt age/geometry from the existing frozen eager samples, and scale three B1 six-row graph groups by each real verification count. These queries have different key lengths, cache residency and scheduling. Ordinary short-key or all-visible shortcuts may avoid an entire index computation; do not add streaming credit there.
